title: Instance migration and GPU affinity: KV-warmup probe across A100/H100/L40S
content:
Summary:
This doc records an exploratory benchmark probing how hypervisor/host-level instance migration and explicit GPU affinity influence KV-cache warmup, short-tail p50/p95 latency, and first-token penalties across three representative GPU classes (NVIDIA A100, H100, and the L40S family) on different cloud SKUs and driver stacks. The goal: identify if host migrations or affinity changes can meaningfully amplify cold-start costs for stateful streaming inference (long KV contexts) and propose mitigations usable in Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments.

Motivation and hypothesis:
- Observed in production: some deployments show occasional per-request first-token spikes after infra-level events (host maintenance, live migration, instance resize).
- Hypotheses: (1) GPU/CPU NUMA affinity shifts and PCIe/NVLink re-probing after migration cause KV cache re-mapping or cache-invalidating DMA behavior; (2) driver/firmware differences across SKUs modulate the severity; (3) prewarming strategies or pinned-affinity policies can materially reduce p95-first-token penalties.

Experiment design (high level):
- Workload: streaming chat decode with prefill 16k tokens (simulates long context state) followed by 1–3 short-turn decodes (32–128 tokens). Emphasized KV cache path and repeated session pattern.
- Platforms tested: three GPU classes mapped to roughly equivalent cloud SKUs: A100 (single-socket 40GB), H100 (PCIe/Hopper), L40S (latest Ampere variant used for inference-like workloads).
- Driver/CUDA matrix: CUDA 11.8, 12.2, 12.3 where available; NVIDIA driver families matching cloud images.
- Migration scenarios simulated:
  1) Cold boot (full VM reboot)
  2) Live host migration (cloud-provider warm migration simulated via suspend/resume + PCI rescan)
  3) CPU-GPU affinity flip (toggle cpuset and rebind process; emulate host NUMA reassign)
  4) Device detach/attach (simulated by unbinding GPU from vfio and rebinding)
- Metrics collected per request: first-token latency, decode per-token p50/p95, KV prefill time, observed PCIe read/write throughput during warmup, kernel-launch rates, and telemetry traces for DMA stub faults. Supplementary: temperature and power telemetry to identify thermal throttles.
- Repeats: each scenario run 20 times per configuration with randomized inter-run idle windows (2–30s) to capture warm/cold transitions.

Environment notes and constraints:
- Tests run in private lab and two cloud regions to capture image/driver variants. Not all driver stacks were available for L40S; where missing we marked as N/A.
- Workload uses Redwood runtime v1.18.3 with experimental PCIe/KV-tracing hooks (feature-flagged).

Key observations (aggregated):
1) Cold boot baseline:
- All GPUs show similar decode p50 once KV is populated, but first-token penalty (prefill+first-decode) varied: H100 median penalty ~160ms higher than A100 on same SKU images; L40S showed the largest variance across images (200–420ms).
- Root cause signal: during cold boot the runtime hits more kernel launch stalls while building attention kernels and populating KV pointers; this maps to expected JIT/cache warming but is consistent across SKUs.

2) Live migration / suspend-resume scenario:
- H100: pronounced p95-first-token spikes in ~60% of runs following resume; packetized DMA reads briefly drop throughput (observed 2–12x transient reduction) for ~150–400ms.
- A100: smaller and shorter perturbations (median 80ms window), fewer p95 events.
- L40S: inconsistent; some images show near-zero impact, others show long 400–700ms tails correlated with PCIe re-enumeration logs in dmesg.
- Trace finding: migrations often cause re-negotiation on PCIe link or driver-level reinitialization of NVLINK pairs; the runtime’s KV pointer table is valid but DMA bandwidth temporarily degrades due to driver queues being drained and re-established.

3) CPU-GPU affinity flip:
- When process affinity was switched off the binding to CPU NUMA nodes changed and the system observed increased latencies if the runtime thread handling DMA ended up on a remote socket relative to the PCIe root complex.
- A100 and H100: p95-first-token increased by 25–60% compared to pinned-affinity baseline in worst cases, with measurable increases in kernel launch latencies (lock contention in host drivers).
- Mitigation: rebinding thread pools to the same NUMA domain as GPU root complex restored baseline.

4) Device detach/attach (simulated hot-swap):
- This had the largest single-run variance. In several L40S images the rebind sequence triggered a one-time firmware handshake that caused a ~1s first-token penalty. H100 showed driver-level reinit but often completed within 300–600ms.
- Recommendations: avoid host-level GPU detach/attach during critical serving windows. If unavoidable, route requests to warm fallback pool.

Driver/CUDA interaction notes:
- CUDA 12.x images often had newer optimizations that reduced kernel compile penalty on cold startup, but some combination of driver version + firmware introduced longer post-migration re-initialization windows.
- No single driver family uniformly dominated; behavior depends on SKU+cloud-image. This underlines the need for runtime-level mitigations rather than relying solely on image pinning.

Operational implications for Redwood products:
- Hosted API: provider-managed migrations make it hard to completely eliminate these rare spikes; recommend exposing a 'migration-safety' route tag that defaults to an internal fallback model/pool during provider maintenance windows.
- Dedicated: give customers an "affinity-safe" configuration recommended for low-latency workloads. This includes CPU/GPU pinning, live-migration avoidance policy, and an optional prewarm agent that issues lightweight KV-touch transactions after any detected host-level event.
- Private: offer a small daemon (opt-in) that watches for PCIe/driver reinit events and proactively issues KV rehydration calls and a short-traffic prefill to amortize first-token penalty.

Mitigations tested and effectiveness:
1) Lightweight KV pre-touch (runtime issues a single small decode touching remote KV pages after migration): reduced median first-token penalty by ~70% in H100 and ~50% in L40S problematic images. Cost: small number of tokens per node per migration event.
2) Affinity pinning as runtime config: eliminated most NUMA-related spikes; requires platform-level cpuset enforcement for container runtimes.
3) Staged request ramp (drain->slow-traffic->normal): effective but has UX cost (requests see reduced concurrency briefly).
4) Fallback to smaller local model or CPU decode: guaranteed stability but higher cost/latency overall.

Recommended next steps and experiments:
- Short-term (1–2 sprints): implement experimental "post-migration pre-touch" feature behind feature flag in runtime; add telemetry events for host-migration detection and pre-touch success/failure. Draft API surface for Dedicated "affinity-safe" profile.
- Medium-term (month): run A/B in Dedicated clusters with affinity pinning + pre-touch to measure real-world event frequency and SLO impact.
- Longer-term: partner with cloud image team to characterize firmware handshake patterns for L40S images and propose image-level knobs to reduce reinit windows.

Limitations and open questions:
- Not all cloud SKUs could be exhaustively tested; results may vary for multi-tenant host environments.
- We emulated some migration behaviors; true provider-level live migration may have additional interactions.
- Further analysis required to correlate thermal/power telemetry and driver reinit windows in large-scale fleet.

Appendix (experiment checklist and quick commands):
- trace flags used: REDWOOD_TRACE_KV=1 REDWOOD_PCI_RESCAN_SIM=1
- affinity commands used: taskset / cset shield scripts (examples attached in internal gist)
- quick reproduction steps: 1) warm model with 16k prefill, 2) suspend/resume VM or trigger PCIe rescan, 3) run 10 short-decode probes and record telemetry.

Concluding note:
This probe highlights that infra-level host events and affinity shifts can produce non-trivial first-token tails even when KV pointers remain valid. Practical mitigations (pre-touch, affinity pinning, staged ramps) show strong returns for low implementation cost and should be prioritized for Dedicated and Private offerings.

Author: Maya Chen (eng-serving-runtime)
Reviewed-by: Ethan Park, Riya Patel
